# Kailash OS Cookbook {#cookbook-home}

This book is the task-oriented companion to the [Kailash OS
guide](https://docs.kailash.tools). Where the guide explains what a
tool **is** (man-style reference pages for the whole catalogue), the
cookbook answers **how do I do X**: every page is a standalone recipe
in the O'Reilly cookbook format —

1. **Problem** — the task, in operator terms
2. **Solution** — the copy-paste-able commands with expected output
   shapes
3. **Discussion** — why it works, what it touches, when to choose an
   alternative
4. **See also** — the matching reference pages and neighbour recipes

Recipes are worked runs, never invented transcripts: output renders as
*shapes* with placeholders, and anything not yet worked against a real
pin stays marked PENDING — the same no-invented-evidence rule the rest
of the project documents follow.

## How the book is organised

- **Sections are themes** — Getting started / Scanning / Attack–defence
  pairs / Ops / Administrator. A recipe keeps its section for life; it
  is never re-parented between sections.
- **Level is metadata, not navigation** — each recipe carries an
  easy/medium/hard level in its header table, displayed on the page
  and counted in the [recipe directory](recipes/directory.qmd).
- **Top-10 collections are generated views** — OWASP ML/LLM/API Top-10
  recipe sets render as generated index pages over recipe tags, they
  never re-organise the book (see the [recipe
  directory](recipes/directory.qmd) for the current coverage).
- **Recipes are technical and grounded** — every command surface is
  quoted from the manifest row (the single source of truth), the
  landed CLI slice, or the pinned upstream source; expected outputs
  render as shapes, never invented transcripts; the mlflow pair
  recipe walks the landed
  `kailash-integration-mlflow-attack` probe pair (see
  [Attack the platform, then verify](recipes/attack-defence/attack-then-verify.qmd)).

## Status

The book is being built in the 2026.01 release window. Wave 1: recipe
template, organisation ADR, one worked exemplar (garak), and grounded
versions of the core setup pages. Wave 2 (in build): the deep recipe
set across all sections, header tables on every page, code-block
spacing, and the directory generator. Progress is tracked on the
repository's issue tracker (cookbook parent: the repo's pinned issue;
wave 2: KA-WS-5.12).
